units.title: Philosophers
units.blurb: Locke, Berkeley, Hume and Kant on knowledge, government and morals.

units.title: Satire
units.blurb: Swift, Voltaire and Diderot laugh at the follies of their age.

units.title: Laws, Society and Wealth
units.blurb: Montesquieu, Rousseau, Adam Smith and the founding papers of the United States.

units.title: History and a Life
units.blurb: Gibbon's fall of Rome and Boswell's Life of Johnson.

topics.title: Locke: Civil Government and Toleration
topics.short: People have rights to life, liberty and property, government rests on their consent, and belief can't be forced.

topics.title: Locke: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding
topics.short: The mind starts as blank paper, and every idea comes from experience: sensation and reflection.

topics.title: Berkeley: The Principles of Human Knowledge
topics.short: To be is to be perceived: a bishop argues there is no matter apart from minds.

topics.title: Hume: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding
topics.short: We never see one thing make another happen; we only learn to expect it. What, then, can we know?

topics.title: Kant: The Critique of Pure Reason
topics.short: What can reason know? Kant answers that the mind shapes experience by its own forms of space, time and cause.

topics.title: Kant: The Moral Philosophy
topics.short: Act only on a rule you could want everyone to follow, and treat people always as ends, never only as means.

topics.title: Kant: The Critique of Judgment
topics.short: What happens when we call something beautiful or sublime, and how we judge purpose in living things.

topics.title: Swift: Gulliver's Travels
topics.short: A ship's doctor among tiny people, giants, floating scientists and talking horses, each a mirror for England.

topics.title: Voltaire: Candide
topics.short: A young man taught that all is for the best meets one disaster after another, and ends by tending his garden.

topics.title: Diderot: Rameau's Nephew
topics.short: A philosopher talks in a Paris café with a brilliant, shameless musician who mocks every virtue.

topics.title: Montesquieu: The Spirit of Laws
topics.short: Laws fit a people's climate, customs and government, and freedom needs separate powers that check each other.

topics.title: Rousseau: The Discourses
topics.short: How did inequality begin? Rousseau tells a story of people in a state of nature and the first fence.

topics.title: Rousseau: The Social Contract
topics.short: 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains': a government is legitimate only by the general will.

topics.title: Adam Smith: The Wealth of Nations
topics.short: The pin factory and the division of labor, markets and prices, and what makes nations grow rich.

topics.title: The American State Papers
topics.short: The founding documents: a declaration of rights, a first league of states, and the Constitution that replaced it.

topics.title: The Federalist
topics.short: Eighty-five newspaper essays explaining and defending the new Constitution, from factions to the courts.

topics.title: Gibbon: The Decline and Fall, I
topics.short: Rome at its height under the good emperors, and the slow troubles that followed.

topics.title: Gibbon: The Decline and Fall, II
topics.short: The empire in the east, the rise of new powers, and the fall of Constantinople in 1453.

topics.title: Boswell: The Life of Samuel Johnson
topics.short: The great biography: a young Scot follows the dictionary maker for twenty years and writes down his talk.

topics.title: Lavoisier: Elements of Chemistry
topics.short: Careful weighing shows that matter is neither made nor lost, oxygen explains burning, and chemistry gets its new names.
topics.trouble: A sealed flask keeps its weight when tin burns inside; it gets heavier only when air rushes in.
